summary: deepseek-flash is the new primary. Two things forced the re-rank: the previous primary's headline en->id figure (84.66) turned out to be a stale testset-v1 number — the balanced-set truth is 73.71 — and bracket-scheme survival is now measured for every candidate with a free-quota verification path. Standing rule: a conclusion here requires (a) [[n]] bracket survival on the current scheme and (b) free-quota verifiability, because no paid credits are held on any optional gateway (only provider free quotas and free promotions are used). gemma-4-31b-it, glm-5 and kimi-k2.5 met neither bar on the current scheme and are dropped from the site entirely. Disqualified below does NOT mean bad at translation — several dropped models topped the quality tables — it means unusable or unverifiable for THIS production pipeline, which masks people's names before translation and restores them afterwards.

why: 10/10 masked-name token survival in both directions on the [[n]] bracket scheme
77.10 chrF id->en — the best measured, +2.25 over glm-5.3-flash and +3.39 over the previous primary
74.42 chrF en->id (2nd overall; only the 6x-pricier qwen3.5-397b edges it)
non-thinking (reasoning disabled): no leakage, 0.74-0.87 s/segment — a 300-segment entry fits the 5-minute cron sequentially

verified within the ~3 chrF cross-provider parity band at three providers: official $0.15/$0.60 per M tokens, OpenRouter $0.0763/$0.1526 (the cheapest token-safe listing measured), Cloudflare $0.44/$1.32 — a 300-segment entry costs two to three cents

alternatives.why: the cheapest safe model ($0.0875/$0.35 per M tokens — about two cents per two-direction sweep) at 1.4-1.6 s/segment, non-thinking, with 10/10 bracket survival verified on first-party QwenCloud (qwen3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507, the same model within the parity band). Demoted because its headline 84.66 en->id was a stale testset-v1 figure: the balanced-set truth is 73.71 both directions, -3.4 chrF id->en vs deepseek-flash

74.85/73.68 chrF (id->en/en->id), 10/10 bracket survival both directions, $0.15/$0.50 per M list — but both known hosts mandate reasoning, so every call bills ~1000+ hidden thinking tokens (effective cost roughly 2-3x list) and Cloudflare's serving runs ~3x slower than OpenRouter's (11.5 vs 4.0 s/sentence)
76.12/74.36 chrF with 10/10 bracket survival both directions — second-best id->en among bracket-verified models, at 3x the flash tier's price ($0.435/$0.87 per M) and ~1.5x its latency

alternatives.role: zero-cost failover tier (with xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash, cohere/command-a-plus, upstage/solar-mini4)
alternatives.why: all four Cline free-promotion models pass 10/10 bracket survival in both directions at $0 — no credits held on any gateway. glm-5.3-prime leads them (74.27 chrF id->en / 72.72 en->id, 2.7-4.4 s/s with reasoning on), mimo-v2.6-flash is close (73.36/72.57); command-a-plus is the fastest hosted model measured (0.9 s/s) but weak id->en (67.14); solar-mini4 trails (71.60/67.33). Mid-field quality — an emergency tier if paid gateways are all unavailable, not a successor. The promos rotate: verify an id still meters zero before relying on it

disqualified.reason: on the [[n]] bracket scheme it survives 10/10 en->id but dropped an intermittent marker id->en (9/10) — much improved from the PUA era (which broke it outright), but a 1-in-20 drop rate keeps it out of the outage-failover seat

their PUA-era survival failures were the token scheme, not the models — on [[n]] brackets the whole qwen-mt family passes 10/10 both directions (re-measured 2026-09-30). They stay out anyway: their plain en->id runs die at QwenCloud's data-inspection filter so no complete quality ranking is possible, the family carries non-raisable rate caps and single-vendor retirement risk, and the production qwen-mt-turbo retires 2026-10-10

same open weights as the full-precision qwen3-30b twin but Cloudflare's fp8 build measures 5.8 chrF below it en->id (67.84 vs 73.65) — quantization damage beyond the ~3 chrF cross-provider parity band, so it is not collapsed and is not a candidate

dropped from the site entirely on 2026-09-30: no free-quota path can verify them on the [[n]] scheme (OpenRouter :free variants are excluded by the account's ZDR/data-training guardrails; Cloudflare, QwenCloud and Cline host only other versions) and no paid credits are held. Their PUA-era runs are archived under results/archive/dropped-2026-09-30; restore from git history if OpenRouter credits arrive

caveats: 2026-09-30 cross-provider parity: identical open-weight models measured at several providers land within ~3 chrF per direction (temperature 0 leaves serving-stack variance; ~0.5 chrF run-to-run nondeterminism on Cloudflare). The site collapses such runs into one row — primary provider's scores, provider badges, cheapest listing in the cost cell (site/tools/models.ts holds the rules)

free-quota-only policy: no paid credits are held on any optional gateway. QwenCloud's first-party free quota covered the qwen bracket backfill; Cline's free promotions meter zero today but rotate (verify an id still meters zero before use); OpenRouter's :free variants are excluded by this account's ZDR/data-training guardrails; OpenCode Zen's free tier rejects non-OpenCode clients outright; Cline's :free nemotron-3.5-lightning hangs past the 180s request timeout and is unusable
QwenCloud's data-inspection filter hard-rejects one FLORES segment en->id (the harness dies there), so QwenCloud plain runs exist for id->en only; the masked set passes

all prices are list (models.dev + provider catalogues, 2026-09-29/30) per M tokens in/out; the site's Cost column shows the cheapest provider per collapsed model — check it before any spending decision, prices drift
the survival assertion + review flags stay regardless of model: the turbo baseline production trusted also failed the adversarial probe set
qwen-mt-turbo retires 2026-10-10; until the switch, it remains the production model

token-safe models run 0.74-4.4 s/segment sequential: a 300-segment entry fits the 5-minute cron on the faster picks (deepseek-flash 0.87, command-a-plus 0.9) but needs 3-4 concurrent requests on the slower ones
